questions.prompt: Which command installs TypeScript as a project build tool?
questions.explanation: TypeScript is a development dependency, installed with npm install --save-dev typescript. You then run it via npx tsc.

questions.prompt: What does the `strict` compiler option do?

options.text: Turns on a family of strict type-checking options, including strictNullChecks
Forces every value to be annotated

questions.explanation: strict is an umbrella switch enabling the strict-checking family (most importantly strictNullChecks). New projects enable it by default; keep it on.

questions.prompt: How do you type-check a project without producing any JavaScript output?
questions.explanation: --noEmit (or "noEmit": true) runs the full type check but writes no .js — the way bundler-based apps use tsc as a checker.

questions.prompt: The file that configures a TypeScript project is called ______.
questions.explanation: tsconfig.json holds the compilerOptions and marks a folder as a TypeScript project. Generate a starter with tsc --init.

questions.prompt: Which are good reasons to run tsc through `npx` rather than a global install? Select all that apply.

options.text: It uses the exact TypeScript version pinned in the project
Everyone on the team and CI compile with the same version
It permanently installs TypeScript on the system
It avoids version drift between machines

questions.explanation: npx runs the project's pinned version, keeping teammates and CI consistent. It does not perform a permanent global install.

questions.prompt: Order the steps to start a new TypeScript project from scratch.
questions.explanation: Initialize the package, add TypeScript, generate a tsconfig, then compile.
